english.title: Make false representation as to royal approval or award etc
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), in the course of a trade or business, namely **(..SPECIFY TRADE OR BUSINESS..), gave a false indication that

(A)_[goods supplied]
(B)_[services supplied]_
(C)_[methods adopted]_

by you, namely **(..SPECIFY GOODS, SERVICES OR METHODS..), were or were of a kind supplied to or approved by His Majesty or a member of the Royal Family
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 12(1) and 18 of the Trade Descriptions Act 1968.

english.notes:
(i) A person shall not be guilty of an offence under section 12(1) or (2) by reason of doing anything that is a commercial practice unless the commercial practice is unfair.
(ii) Regarding the time limit for prosecutions, section 19(1) states 'No prosecution for an offence under this Act shall be commenced after the expiration of three years from the commission of the offence or one year from its discovery by the prosecutor, whichever is the earlier.'
(iii) Section 19(2) states 'Notwithstanding anything in section 127(1) of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980, a magistrates' court may try an information for an offence under this Act if the information was laid at any time within twelve months from the commission of the offence.'
(iv) Section 19(4)(a) states 'Subsections (2) and (3) .... do not apply where .... the offence was committed by the making of an oral statement ....'.
(v) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the prescribed sum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 19

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
